newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends softer in choppy trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends softer in choppy trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar continued its softer streak on Thursday to close at C$1.3467 (US$0.7426) from Wednesday's close at C$1.3450 (US$0.7435) in choppy trading, dealers said. * They said comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan were positive for the Canadian dollar, helping to limit the day's weakness.
But comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan helped stop the slide of the Canadian dollar, traders said.
Greenspan argued that the Consumer Price Index, which is currently used as the basis for cost-of-living changes, overstates inflation by 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points a year.
The comment encouraged the Canadian currency market to believe the Federal Reserve would not move to raise interest rates at its meeting in early February, dealers said.
Stagnant U.S. rates would benefit the Canadian dollar, so the positive sentiment helped the currency slightly today, they said.
The Canadian dollar's direction on Friday will likely depend on gross domestic product data expected in both Canada and the United States, traders said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar eased to 1.2151 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.2221 marks and slid to 90.35 yen from 90.68 yen.
